title: Vic Dickenson and Edmund Hall
summary: Dickenson embodied jazz humor; Edmund Hall led the Savoy house band and still felt chills next to Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Did you encounter Vic Dickenson in Boston?

Oh, my gosh, Vic Dickenson played the Savoy often. One of the pleasures of jazz to me is its humor, its wit. Vic Dickenson embodied that. He was a quiet, reticent sort of guy, but I wish I had gotten to know him better, because what there was in the music was a man of considerable depth.

Edmund I got to know very well. He led the house band there for a long time. Of course he was a bridge from New Orleans. He grew up in a town near there. He was part of the New Orleans scene. He also – he reminds me of this time with Louis Armstrong. He was with the All Stars for a while. He said something to me. They often played the same repertory almost night after night after night. I didn’t quite have the nerve to say, doesn’t it get boring? But when he said to me – I forget the context – he said, “I still get the chills sometimes standing next to Louis, hearing what he’s doing.” I figured, wow.
